## Context

A mid-size software company offered me a 10-week paid internship for summer, the kind
of role that sometimes converts to a full-time offer. I have heavy coursework and two
exams in the fall term. The offer pays well for an internship but not enough to cover
a full lost summer.

## Options

**Accept the internship**
- 10 weeks, roughly 40 hours a week
- Around 2,200 dollars
- Real production code and a team review process
- Not guaranteed to continue past summer

**Decline, keep the summer for coursework**
- Full summer available for classes and exam prep
- No income
- Repeat the same offer next year if it comes back
- No production experience

## Decision

Accepted. The career impact weight was high, the pay covered the opportunity cost of
summer work, and I believed the internship would convert into a full-time offer.

## Outcome

Reviewed 2026-10-05. Result: worse.

The conversion assumption was simply wrong. There was one intern slot for conversion
and it went to someone who had been there for two previous summers. I was told
early that my team was not hiring, which in hindsight means I should have negotiated
for a different scope or a return offer in writing.

The second failed assumption was that I could still prepare for the fall exams in
August. The project had a hard launch in mid-August and working reasonable hours was
already the expectation. I studied on nights and weekends and arrived for the fall term
behind on two courses. The work itself was good and the technical interview I got
through it led to a second internship offer, but the objective I set for it, the
conversion, did not happen, and the exam prep was a real cost. I would take it again
only if a return offer were in writing.
